Anything that changes behavior or breaks a documented contract is ⚠️ IMPORTANT or 🚨 BLOCKING. The 4-tier census (`issueCounts`) counts posted threads + digest lines and drives the machine verdict — keep it consistent with the inlineComments severities. ### outputs/pr_review_candidates-.json — pool specialist sessions only A pool specialist session (its prompt file present) answers with candidates, never a verdict — the posting review mints the verdict; the aggregation merges, the filter verifies and the posting review posts. The record schema adds the head binding: ```json { "reviewer": "security", "head": "", "count": 2, "truncated": false, "at": "", "candidates": [ {"id": 1, "path": "src/auth/UserService.js", "line": 45, "severity": "BLOCKING", "claim": "User query at line 45 concatenates req.body.user straight into the SQL string; parameterize the statement."}, {"id": 2, "path": "docs/migration.md", "line": null, "severity": "SUGGESTION", "claim": "The rollback path for the new columns is undocumented — a bad deploy cannot revert cleanly."} ] } ``` Rules: `head` = the round head sha from the prompt (a stale file never feeds a newer head); `id` = position in the file; `path` repo-relative; `line` = the diff line or `null` for a digest candidate; `claim` = the substance (no severity header, no verdict language). Severity boundary identical to the verdict tiers above. Nothing else gets written (no pr_review.json, no comment files) and nothing gets posted — worked examples of the claim voice live in each reviewer's few-shots file. ## lens.md # Generalist Review Lens (the base reviewer) The generalist lens: full-diff review across every dimension. The reviewer-agnostic contract (input reading order, output rules, verdict rules, registry protocol, formatting) lives in `instructions/pr_review/base/` and is assembled around this lens — this file is WHAT the base reviewer hunts, not how it answers. ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, review_policy.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Deep read:
first round — every changed file;
re-review (pr_new_hunks.txt present) —
new hunks + interaction neighborhood
(unchanged lines frozen)"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION / NIT
(severity census gates approval per review_policy.md)"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Necessity pass:
threads only for findings that defend
correctness / security / data loss / CI / ticket contract —
everything else → ranked digest"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: does each candidate finding pass the §7 necessity test (defends correctness on a touched path, security, data loss, CI breakage, or the ticket contract) — or is it digest material? ## 3. Changed-file deep read — and frozen already-reviewed code Do not review from the diff alone. **First review round** (no `pr_new_hunks.txt` in the input folder) — read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact **Re-review rounds** (`pr_new_hunks.txt` present — the hunks added since the last reviewed head) — read the full content of the files the new hunks touch plus their interaction neighborhood (direct callers/callees of changed symbols), not whole files. Already-reviewed lines are **frozen**: a finding on an unchanged line is valid only when the new hunks make the problem worse (the interaction test — e.g. a new call path now feeds unvalidated input into old code). Anything else on frozen lines is advisory digest at most (§7), never a thread. If `pr_new_hunks.txt` is absent from a later round (e.g. a force-push the machine could not diff), the whole diff is in scope again. ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ### Delegate to the measured gates Complexity, duplication and style are already measured by the repo's CI — the CRAP ratchet, the duplication gate, lint. The gate is the reviewer of record for those dimensions: a passing gate is not a thread (the cost was already measured and accepted); a failing gate is CI breakage (🚨 BLOCKING). Raise a complexity/duplication/style finding only when no gate covers it **and** the concrete cost is stateable — what breaks or what the next change pays. ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement to the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape). Does not block merge. - **NIT** — changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented: style, formatting, naming micro-preferences. Never blocks merge, never triggers a lap. When in doubt, classify lower and state what evidence would raise the finding one level (the same discipline as the external-spec citation rule below — an unproven claim must not hold a PR hostage). ### Density control — post top-K, digest the overflow `review_policy.md` in the input folder carries the resolved policy and its density cap (`allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8)` — 20→3 · 50→4 · 200→5 · 800→8): - The cap applies to 💡 SUGGESTION / 🪶 NIT threads only — 🚨/⚠️ findings are **never capped** and always post as threads. - Rank your 💡/🪶 findings by value and post only the top-K as inline threads. - The overflow becomes a **ranked digest list** in the general comment (one line each: `path:line — finding`). - The census counts posted threads + digest lines (`issueCounts.suggestions`/`nits` count posts, `digest` counts the overflow lines). - The machine audits the posted thread count against the cap (warn only — it never fails the leg). ### Downgrade protocol — honor a justified ⚠️→💡 from rework A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification in the census** (its thread reply and response summary). When the justification is present, classify the finding 💡 in this round's census — a false-⚠️ review converges to APPROVE without a code change. A silent downgrade does not exist: without the written justification, keep ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (for example, a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source does not contain when the reviewed code is behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - **Before emitting a spec-claim finding without a citation, locate the requirement in the ticket and cite it (for example `ticket.md:12`) — an uncited true claim is demoted mechanically.** - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. The machine applies the same discipline (and a safety net against coin-flip formatting): every uncited spec claim is cross-checked against the ticket text the run already has under `input/`. When the requirement is verifiably present there, the finding keeps 🚨 BLOCKING force and the matched citation is auto-appended; when the ticket contradicts it, lacks it, or the mechanical check is inconclusive, the finding is demoted and stamped `demoted-from-BLOCKING` — the finding-identity registry keeps it re-elevatable in a later round by adding a citation instead of raising the same defect as new. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Necessity test — what earns a thread A thread is expensive: each one costs a rework lap — 15–20 CI minutes — and the rework's own fresh hunks get reviewed again next round. A finding earns a thread only if it **defends** one of: - correctness on a path the change actually touches - security - data loss - CI breakage - the ticket contract Everything else — real, accurate, but not merge-relevant — goes to the **ranked digest list** in the general comment (one line each: `path:line — finding`), never a thread. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists — classify everything you found; only the necessity test decides thread vs digest. - The exhaustive pass keeps running (§3 defines its scope). Re-read the in-scope code and ask: *"What else does this change put at risk?"* — not *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify each thread you are about to open passes the necessity test; everything else is already in the digest. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ## few_shots.md Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":20,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md","severity":"NIT"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1,"nits":1} } ``` **Severity boundary (4 tiers)**: a 🪶 NIT changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented (style, naming, formatting, micro-symmetry); a 💡 SUGGESTION changes clarity of the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape). Anything that changes behavior or breaks a documented contract is ⚠️ IMPORTANT or 🚨 BLOCKING. ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` ## review_verdict_rules.md # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings into 4 tiers: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — clarity of the documented/behavioral surface: missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape. - 🪶 **NIT** — changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented: style, formatting, naming micro-preferences. Then map to the verdict (the machine recomputes it from the census — `postPRReviewComments` treats your token as advisory): | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | Any ⚠️ IMPORTANT (no 🚨) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` (gates approval — policy default) | | Only 💡 / 🪶 remain | `APPROVE` — the cycle converges | **Downgrade protocol:** when the rework lap downgraded a specific ⚠️ to 💡 **with a written justification in the census** (the thread reply states why the finding is not maintainability debt), classify that finding 💡 in this round's census — the false-⚠️ review converges to APPROVE without a code change. Without the written justification, keep ⚠️: a silent downgrade does not exist, and the machine recomputes the verdict from the census you post. `APPROVE` with remaining 💡/🪶 findings is the expected terminal state (the resolved policy's `allowApproveWithSuggestions` derives from the tier table — SUGGESTION rounds polish, NIT rounds none): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. An open ⚠️ **does** gate approval unless the project's `reviewPolicy` explicitly weakens it (owner standing-approval doctrine, epic §4.4). ## Anti-patterns - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, doc-comment refs). A cycle with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`. - ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+. - ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text. The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict. - ❌ 🚨 BLOCKING driven by an uncited external-spec claim ("the spec says X" without a `file:line` / doc URL the leg actually read). Downgrade it to a ⚠️ question; the machine treats BLOCKING threads as ground truth and arms rework on them. (Note: the post-action also downgrades such findings mechanically — keep the JSON consistent with the demoted severity so the census cross-check stays clean.) - ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff — add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead. ## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane `chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride the lane independently). Removing it from a release bump or pin PR strands that PR behind the standard queue. - ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other PR untouched. dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ## bash_tools.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph USE["Use dmtools skill"] U1["Jira, Figma, Confluence, Teams, etc."] U2["Credentials preconfigured via environment variables"] end subgraph SHELLSTATE["⚠️ Persistent-shell pitfalls (sandbox-observed)"] P1["Never end commands with exit — it kills the shell session, making read_bash fail with Invalid shell ID"] P2["Capture the exit code via $? right after the command, before running anything else — a late $? reads the wrong command's code"] P3["Avoid $PIPESTATUS — it produced wrong exit codes in the sandbox; redirect output to a file and check $? instead"] end subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"] C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"] C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). A foreground sleep pins the tool-call open — owner steering and cancel cannot reach you until it ends — and burns wall-clock plus a runner slot"] B3["While a background job runs, keep working on other steps — check progress between steps with bash_job status / bash_job output <job-id> — never park the turn in a watch loop"] B4["A harness hint like background candidate: bash background: true, job board /tasks, --wait-for-jobs is an ORDER, not a suggestion — obey it and start the command in the background; working around it with foreground sleeps is a violation"] B5["Verification order: finalize ALL code edits BEFORE launching a long verification run (full suite, coverage) — verification must run against a frozen tree, otherwise the run is wasted"] B6["Files changed while a verification run is in flight? Do NOT kill it mid-flight — let it finish, treat the result as stale, then deliberately start a fresh run against the updated tree"] B7["B6 covers a job still making progress — do NOT kill it mid-flight; a job with NO progress for ~10 min (or 2× its expected duration) is HUNG — dispose of it and MOVE ON: bash_job stop <job-id>, note the disposal in the deliverable (job id, command, last output tail), finish the remaining steps and write outputs/response.md reporting the unverified part. ## PR Description

Implements #1503 (estimate-based adaptive mode selection for dev legs). Part of epic #1440.

## What

Dev legs now self-select their working mode: after surveying the ticket, the agent estimates the work and works by a written plan when the estimate crosses a configurable threshold — no human mode setting, no reliance on ticket text.

- **`js/common/developmentModeAdaptive.js`** (new) — threshold resolution (`developmentModeConfig.adaptive.planThreshold`, default 3, any positive integer — the scale is open-ended; zero/negative/non-integer → warn + default), decision-record parsing (fail-safe to null), the adaptive appendix text + materialization, shadow-mode carry-over from gh-1437.
- **`js/conditions/isDevelopmentModeAdaptive.js`** (new) — the adaptive conditional cliPrompts entry; `isDevelopmentModePlan.js` no longer admits adaptive legs (the plan appendix file on adaptive legs is an escalation READ target only).
- **`js/preCliDevelopmentSetup.js`** — adaptive materializes the adaptive appendix + the plan escalation read (resolve-both-before-write so a failed resolution leaves no orphan files); the gh-1437 pre-leg signal routing is retired from this wiring and the signal extractor + calibration harness are deleted outright (the routing decision belongs to the agent, in-leg).
- **`js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js`** — informational `dev-plan-escalated` label stamped from `outputs/<KEY>/scope_estimate.json` (mode=plan); same degrade-not-fail discipline as `ai_concerns`. Bug legs delegate to the same action — one seam covers both.
- **`story_development.json` / `bug_development.json`** — `developmentMode: "adaptive"`, `planThreshold: 3`; the adaptive entry last in the base cliPrompts. The dynamic-repo template stays `default` (consumer repos opt in per the issue).
- **`docs/development-mode.md`** + human/generated agent docs — §2.3 rewritten (in-leg estimate decision), config surface, estimate-routing calibration section (decision-log offline replay), invariant correction.

## Decision record

The agent writes only what it holds at decision time — `{sp, threshold, mode, reason, outcome}` — one JSON line in the existing per-leg `outputs/` convention. `model` and legs-per-ticket are NOT agent-written: the harness usage line already carries the model; the leg count is derived offline from those lines. Zero new infrastructure.

## Evidence

Paired calibration run (15 tasks × forced direct/plan legs, production model): SP 1–2 neutral; plan net-positive from SP 3; at the top bands plan cost −33..47% fewer requests/tokens, +13% tests written, and no leg lost to the job wall (direct lost one). Crossover → default threshold 3 SP (config knob).
